summary: Monolith's No One Lives Forever series is a stylish spy FPS lineage whose first game remains trapped in rights and digital-availability limbo.

entries.title: The Operative: No One Lives Forever
entries.definitive_edition: Owned Windows Game of the Year Edition, with PS2 flashback levels documented separately if needed

emulation.notes: Use native Windows compatibility fixes/Modernizer where needed; use PCSX2 only for PS2-exclusive comparison if a legally sourced copy is available.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Patched owned Windows GOTY retail route

primary.version: Owned Game of the Year Edition or patched retail release
primary.why: The Windows release is the original route and the Game of the Year Edition adds the official Rest and Relaxation mission. The game is not sold through normal digital storefronts because of unresolved rights, so the honest archive route is an owned retail/GOTY copy with modern compatibility patches documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned Windows retail or Game of the Year copy. Record edition, patch/Modernizer state, widescreen/FOV/audio fixes, mission, difficulty, intelligence item completion, multiplayer availability, and whether PS2-exclusive flashback levels were sampled separately.

secondary.exclusive_content: Three exclusive Cate Archer flashback levels
secondary.what_to_play: Sample after the PC route if completeness across versions matters.
secondary.why: The PS2 port lacks PC multiplayer and the GOTY Rest and Relaxation mission, but adds unique flashback content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not point users to unofficial downloads as the primary route; document owned-copy provenance and compatibility patches.
